result:
Fixed the bug in `src/jinja2/idtracking.py`'s `Symbols.branch_update`.

**Root cause**: the old code had an optimization that, when a name was already stored in the outer scope before an `if`, skipped tracking it entirely per-branch â€” and separately, when a name was stored in *all* branches of an if/elif/else, skipped forcing a reload. Combined, this meant a variable set in all three branches while never referenced beforehand was left with a stale `undefined` load instead of picking up the real value, since the "all branches covered" case was treated as "no update needed" rather than "still needs to load."

**Fix** (matching the real upstream Jinja fix, commit `66587ce9`): replaced the branch-count bookkeeping with a simpler set-difference approach â€” collect all names stored across branches, subtract names already stored in the outer scope, and then always resolve/alias every remaining name, regardless of whether it was set in all branches or just some.

Changes:
- `src/jinja2/idtracking.py` â€” the actual fix
- `tests/test_regression.py` â€” added `test_load_parameter_when_set_in_all_if_branches`, reproducing the exact edge case (a name referenced then set in all three branches of `if`/`elif`/`else`)
- `CHANGES.rst` â€” changelog entry

Verified: the new test and the full existing suite pass (only unrelated pre-existing collection errors in `test_async.py`/`test_async_filters.py` due to a missing `attrs` package for `trio`, not caused by this change).
